name: Itaú Unibanco (Brazil bank)
money: Lending (net interest ~R$33B/quarter), fees (cards, asset mgmt), insurance. Loan book ~R$1.5 trillion.
moat: Cheapest funding in Brazil (millions of accounts), best underwriting (overdue loans ~half the market's), very efficient (spends 37 cents per R$1 of revenue).
record: Recurring profit R$46.8B in 2025 (+13%); ROE 19-23% every year; Q3 2026 R$12.6B (+6.7%), ROE 23.6%.
strength: Capital ratio (CET1) 12.7% - extra cushion; bad loans 2.0%; strong liquidity.
risks: 1) Brazil 2027 slowdown - Itaú itself expects tougher credit. 2) Brazilian real falling vs US$. 3) Fintech competition + Brazil taxes (10% withholding on dividends to foreigners from 2026).
scenarios: Bear ~-3% to 0%/yr · Base ~8-10%/yr · Bull ~14-16%/yr (5 years, from US$7.34)
canada: Buy NYSE ADR 'ITUB' in US$ (use your USD to avoid 1.5% FX fee). Brazil tax on dividends is lost in a TFSA; claimable in non-registered.
why: Highest-quality bank of the group at ~9x earnings. Brazil + currency risk = start with a half-size position; add only if 2027 credit holds up or price falls further.

name: CGI (Montreal IT services)
verdict: ✅ BUY SMALLER (half size, at buy price)
money: Running clients' IT systems on multi-year contracts (55%) + consulting/systems projects (45%). Revenue C$16.6B.
moat: Switching costs - governments/banks can't easily replace who runs their core systems. C$32B backlog (~2 years of revenue).
record: Revenue C$12.1B (2021) -> C$16.6B (2026); EPS C$6.04 -> C$8.58 (~9%/yr); steady 11% net margin; ~C$2.1B free cash flow/yr.
strength: Net debt ~C$3.8B (rising, used for buybacks) but manageable vs C$2.5B/yr cash flow.
risks: 1) AI shrinking paid IT hours (stock fell ~40% on this). 2) Organic growth only ~2%; EPS helped by debt-funded buybacks. 3) Government spending cuts / losing big contracts.
canada: Buy 'GIB.A' on TSX in C$ - no FX fee, no foreign tax. Best in TFSA.
why: Clear quality business at ~10-11x earnings if it hits C$91; AI question unanswered = start half size and add if growth improves. Don't chase at today's price.

name: Evertz Technologies (broadcast tech, Ontario)
money: Equipment + software to route/control live TV video; ~47% repeat software/services; 71% US/Canada.
moat: Switching costs in live broadcast facilities; heavy R&D (~29% of revenue).
record: Revenue ~C$441M -> C$516M in 5 yrs; profit flat (~C$64-72M); dividend raised every year (now C$0.82, ~8.5% yield at buy price).
strength: Little debt, BUT cash nearly gone after a special dividend; dividend now ≈ earnings.
risks: 1) Dividend safety (Q1 EPS C$0.10 vs C$0.205 dividend). 2) Broadcasters shrinking / moving to cloud. 3) Margins slipping, tariffs.
canada: TSX 'ET' in C$, no foreign tax; TFSA ideal; use limit orders (founders own ~65%).
why: Cheap, founder-owned, high yield - but flat profits and thin cash. Small position only at C$9.61; check December results first.

name: Corby Spirit & Wine (J.P. Wiser's, Pernod Ricard Canada)
verdict: ✅ BUY SMALLER (income holding, at buy price)
money: Own Canadian brands (81%: Wiser's, Polar Ice, Cottage Springs/Nude cocktails) + commissions selling Pernod brands (Absolut, Jameson) + exports.
moat: Known brands + exclusive Pernod agency + liquor-board shelf access (hard for newcomers).
record: Revenue C$159M -> C$272M (helped by acquisition); profit ~+9%/yr; dividend now C$1.00 (~8.9% yield at buy price).
risks: 1) FY26 boosted by US liquor pulled from shelves - reversing. 2) People drinking less; growth ~1%. 3) Pernod controls it + charges fees.
canada: TSX 'CSW.A' in C$, eligible Canadian dividends; TFSA fits; thin trading - limit orders.
why: Steady dividend payer, cheap at buy price, but little growth and Pernod control. Small income position only.

name: Ambev (Brazil beer, AB InBev)
money: Brazil beer (46%: Skol, Brahma, Stella), rest of Latin America, Labatt Canada, soft drinks.
moat: Wide: dominant Brazil beer share, unmatched distribution to ~1M small bars/shops, low costs, 34% EBITDA margin.
record: Revenue/profit ~+5%/yr in reais (2021-25); Q3 2026 normalized EPS +15%; but US$ returns hurt by falling real.
strength: Lots of cash, ~R$20B+/yr free cash flow. Hidden: ~R$33.5B disputed tax claims (not provisioned).
risks: 1) Weak beer volumes + Heineken price competition. 2) Brazilian real / Argentina currency. 3) Brazil taxes (10% dividend withholding) + tax disputes.
scenarios: Bear ~1-3%/yr · Base ~12-15%/yr · Bull ~18-20%/yr (from US$1.94, in US$)
canada: NYSE 'ABEV' in US$ (use USD); Brazil withholding lost in TFSA -> non-registered better.
why: Best moat of the group, but currency + tax eat returns. Small slice only at US$1.94.

name: BBVA (Spain bank, mostly Mexico)
money: Mexico (largest bank there), Spain, Turkey, South America.
moat: Medium: #1 in Mexico, very efficient, strong digital banking.
record: Profit ~€4.7B (2021) -> €10.5B (2025); dividend raised 31% for 2025; big buybacks.
risks: 1) Turkey hyperinflation + provisions (stock -5% on Oct 29). 2) Spain profits stalled (lower rates + bank tax). 3) Mexico slowdown/peso.
canada: NYSE 'BBVA' in US$; Spain withholds 19% (treaty 15%) - lost in TFSA.
why: Good bank but not on sale yet, and stacks Turkey + Mexico + Spain risks. Itaú is the better discounted bank. Revisit if it drops to ~US$21.
